rows: Here is the plan. Grip, then move, then hold. You have until the bell.
I brawl when the sea gets rough. Calm water is better.
Nerve is a wave that comes in. Get out of its way or be knocked over.
Slow water is fine too. Time does not hurry for anybody.
The people came for something that holds. Throw them a line.
I am tied down, and I am not coming loose.
I earn my place on the main event. Nobody hands it to me.
Check your footing before the swell. Steady on your feet.
Technique is a knot. Tie it properly. Show me one hold you have tied off properly.
Strikes are a rough patch. Keep your footing or go under.
Nerve is only sound if you can get back to safety.
A stall drifts. I do not drift.
The people deserve a contest that goes somewhere. Give them the course.
You question my reliability. Watch me hold under pressure, then say it again.
You are proud of your {strength}, and it had better hold in a swell. Fine. Show me it holds under pressure.
I have looked at your {strength}. It is fine in calm water. Not in a storm.
Steady on your feet, I see. Well steadied. Calm water helps everybody.
Noted. We have the same course, then.
I could shout about that. I would rather keep my footing.
One fall, one knot. Keep me down by the bell. Simple.
On the mat, I hold the line until I say otherwise.
Grounded or standing, I am still where I was.
Keep your eyes on my approach. I will come to you, and you will not like it.
That knot will hold. It holds.
Still no line thrown back. Answer before the moment turns.
Noted. That is a point I will keep.
Understood. We sort the rest out at the bell.
I will hold this match to the finish, and I will not let go early.
My approach is plain. I say the plan, then I stick to it.
Whatever happens, you will know where I stood, and it will be the same place tomorrow.
We are still at sea. The moment is still moving.
I have one instruction left. You will get it at the bell.
I don't tie a knot to nothing. If I can't back the charge up, I won't hold you to it.
You've asked for something solid. I haven't got it. Let that line go.
Good. We don't need that loose end dragging behind us in the match.
That'll hold. Leave the unsupported bit ashore and meet me in the ring.
Watch where we put our weight and how we get free. The proof's in the work, not the talk.
We'll see what holds together when the pressure comes on. That's something nobody needs to take on trust.
Leave the rumour ashore. What can we show the people when the pressure comes on in that ring?
What part of our wrestling can we put to the test when neither of us gives ground?
You have a course plotted around my {strength}. Keep your footing when the water gets rough.
Knowing about my {strength} gives you something to steer by. It won't keep you steady when I put them to work.
Agreed. No anchor for that claim. We let it go.
Point taken. Mark the position we actually know, not the one we hoped to reach.
You've sailed these waters before. That doesn't tell you where I'll turn next.
Years at sea count for something, but you've still got to steer through this particular contest.
Experience is knowing which way to shift your weight when the water gets rough.
A change of current doesn't mean I forget how to steer. That's what the years have taught me.
